newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares stage late recovery after early fall.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares stage late recovery after early fall.

text.p: Blue chips at Bombay bourses rallied smartly from intra-day lows on Wednesday in a roller coaster session marked by heavy speculative action in select stocks, dealers said.
"This is a big speculative game. Operators are trying to sway fickle market sentiments ahead of the budget," said a local dealer. The 1997/98 (April-March) budget is due on February 28.

The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) rallied 59.48 points, or 1.71 percent from the day's low of 3,468.89 to 3,528.37. It finished with a net loss of 1.86 points over Tuesday's close.
Analysts say the government will have to tackle a burgeoning fiscal deficit, announce incentives for growth-affected sectors and come out with reforms to shore up capital markets.
But, political compulsions might force Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party centre-left coalition government to come out with half-hearted measures, dealers said.
"One has to display some cautiousness ahead of the budget," said dealer Rasesh Maniar at brokers Mukesh Babu.
Shares of ACC gained 66.75 rupees on active speculative buying aided by heavy purchases by foreign funds. The stock was among the top market outperformers with 221,975 shares traded.
"The late rally might prompt a firm Thursday start," said a dealer. SBI rose 0.50 rupees to 289.25 and ITC 1.25 to 417.50.
India's Congress party said on Wednesday that it will not immediately move to topple the United Front government it has reluctantly supported for nine months.

"It won't fall this year," Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil told Reuters when asked if Gowda's government might fall during the three-month long parliament's budget session which opens on Thursday. Gowda has fewer than 200 deputies in the 545-member lower house of parliament. Congress controls some 140 deputies.
